about: Small mid-run plan with a fan of three parallel tasks, one of every task status, an open, an answered and a withdrawn question, and a draft PR.

run/main.title: CSV export of print-on-demand orders
run/main.objective: Add a CSV export of print-on-demand orders to the order-tracking app so the warehouse stops retyping them into the label printer software. Warehouse staff pick a date range and download one file.
run/main.approach: Write the CSV in one small module that streams rows from a single query, so a month of orders never sits in memory. The download endpoint and the button both sit on top of it. The whole feature stays behind a feature flag until the warehouse has tried it.
run/main.delivery: One PR, feature/pod-order-csv-export, into main. The owner merges.

done_check.text: A warehouse user can download a CSV of orders for a date range from the orders page
The file opens in Excel with accented names intact
done_check.note: Needs a real Excel check on the warehouse laptop.

done_check.text: Every export is recorded with who ran it and the range

out_of_scope: Pushing orders to the printer software directly
risks: Address lines with embedded newlines can break the printer software's import
A year-wide export on the production database could be slow; the range is capped at 92 days

tasks/T1.title: Column spec and CSV writer
tasks/T1.goal: Streaming CSV writer with the warehouse's column order.
tasks/T1.verify: Unit tests with a fixture of 20 rows, including " and , in a title.
tasks/T1.approach: Write CsvWriter over a row iterator, csv.writer with \r\n line ends, header row first. Columns come from a list in orders/export/columns.py, so changing the order is a one-line edit.
tasks/T1.outcome: Added CsvWriter and columns.py. Prefixes any cell starting with =, +, - or @ with a quote, which the plan didn't mention.

tasks/T2.title: Feature flag
tasks/T2.goal: Add a feature flag for the export, off by default.
tasks/T2.verify: Flag read in tests and in the template helper.
tasks/T2.outcome: Flag lives in settings/flags.py, default off. Staging override set in deploy/staging.env.

tasks/T3.title: GET /orders/export.csv endpoint
tasks/T3.goal: Stream the file for a date range.
tasks/T3.verify: Request tests for a good range, a 93-day range, and a user outside the group.
tasks/T3.approach:
Query pod_orders joined to addresses with .iterator(chunk_size=500), wrap in StreamingHttpResponse. Reject ranges over 92 days with a 400. Filename quillmere-orders-<from>-<to>.csv.

Permission is the existing warehouse group.

tasks/T4.title: Split shipping address into printer columns
tasks/T4.goal: Name, line 1, line 2, city, postcode, country as the label software wants them.
tasks/T4.verify: Tests with a three-line address and a name containing ø and Nguyễn.
tasks/T4.approach: The printer software chokes on newlines inside a cell, so collapse them to a space and put overflow into line2.

tasks/T5.title: Export audit log
tasks/T5.goal: Record who exported what, and when.
tasks/T5.verify: Migration applies and reverses cleanly; a row exists after an export.
tasks/T5.approach: New table order_export_runs (user_id, range_from, range_to, row_count, created_at), written once the response has finished streaming, not when it starts. Migration 0042_order_export_runs.

tasks/T6.title: Nightly drop to the warehouse share
tasks/T6.goal: Write yesterday's file to the warehouse's SFTP folder each night.
tasks/T6.verify: A scheduled job writes a file that the warehouse can see.
tasks/T6.blocked_on: Warehouse IT creating the SFTP account for the app and sending its host key. Tomás has asked, with no date yet.
tasks/T6.approach: Waits on warehouse IT creating the SFTP account for the app and sending the host key (asked by Tomás, no date yet). Once we have it the job is a few lines in jobs/nightly_export.py.

tasks/T7.title: Export button and date picker on the orders page
tasks/T7.verify: Button is hidden when the flag is off; click downloads a file for the chosen range.

tasks/T8.title: XLSX variant
tasks/T8.goal: Same export as an Excel workbook.
tasks/T8.verify: Workbook opens with the same columns.
tasks/T8.approach: Would use openpyxl and a second writer sharing columns.py.
tasks/T8.outcome: Dropped after Q1: the warehouse is happy with CSV.

questions/Q1.title: CSV, XLSX, or both?
questions/Q1.context: The warehouse retypes orders into the label software today. The software imports CSV, but Nguyễn mentioned some staff open files in Excel first to check them.

options.label: CSV only
options.cost: Excel may garble accents unless we write a UTF-8 byte order mark.

options.label: CSV and XLSX
options.cost: A second writer and its tests, about two days.

questions/Q2.title: Which order statuses does the export include by default?
questions/Q2.context: The orders page lists paid, printing, shipped and refunded orders. The warehouse only prints from paid ones, but Tomás thinks shipped ones are useful when a parcel is lost.

options.label: Paid only
options.cost: Lost-parcel reprints need a second export with a filter we haven't built.

options.label: A status checklist on the page

questions/Q3.title: Does the export need the tracking number?
questions/Q3.context: Unclear whether the label software wants the carrier tracking number as an input column.
questions/Q3.answer: Withdrawn: the sample import has no tracking column.

journal/2026-10-12T09:15:00Z.text: Plan written from the spec: eight tasks, one PR.

journal/2026-10-12T15:30:00Z.text: Withdrew the tracking-number question. The label software's sample import in the spec has no such column, so T1 uses the spec's list.

journal/2026-10-13T07:50:00Z.text: CSV is enough, XLSX not needed.

journal/2026-10-13T08:40:00Z.text: Took the plan. T8 dropped per Q1. Will write a UTF-8 BOM so Excel shows accents; T1 already has the hook.

journal/2026-10-13T10:20:00Z.text: T1 and T2 started in parallel; they touch different files.

journal/2026-10-13T14:05:00Z.text: T1 merged into the feature branch. Reviewer flagged formula injection (cells starting with =); added a quote prefix, which the plan hadn't covered.

journal/2026-10-13T15:30:00Z.text: T2 merged. Opened the draft PR now that something has landed.

journal/2026-10-14T09:10:00Z.text: T3, T4 and T5 can run together, all depend only on T1 or T2. Started all three.

journal/2026-10-14T16:00:00Z.text: Asked the warehouse IT contact for an SFTP account; T6 is blocked until it exists.

journal/2026-10-15T11:25:00Z.text: T5 review found the audit row is written before the stream ends, so a failed download still counts. Sent back to fix.

journal/2026-10-15T14:10:00Z.text: Asked Q2. T7 waits on it; nothing else does.

journal/2026-10-16T13:50:00Z.text: T4 in review. T3 half done.
